failing_checks.title: Per-action amount bound
failing_checks.reason: The client signs a SAC transfer for whatever amount the challenge states. There is no maximum, no allowlist and no approval hook. onProgress is only a notification. The channel client signs the requested cumulative amount the same way.

failing_checks.title: Cumulative budget
failing_checks.reason: No cumulative or session budget exists on the client. The server-side store tracks only challenge ids and channel cumulative totals, and it is optional.

failing_checks.title: Atomic budget accounting
failing_checks.reason: The read of the previous cumulative and the later put are separated by an awaited simulation. The check and the update are not atomic. The charge replay check is also a separate get and put.

failing_checks.title: Recipient binding
failing_checks.reason: The client takes the recipient and currency from the server-supplied challenge. It does not check them against an operator allowlist.

failing_checks.title: Asset identity and units
failing_checks.reason: Both the contract id and the BigInt amount are compared in verifyFromRawOps. In push mode, verifySacTransfer returns without error if the envelope is missing or fails to parse. failing_checks.title: Replay and double payment
failing_checks.reason: Replay protection runs only if a store is configured. It keys on the challenge id and not on the tx hash. The same on-chain payment hash can therefore satisfy many challenges with the same amount and recipient.

failing_checks.title: Incoming payment verification
failing_checks.reason: The recipient, contract and amount are checked, but the check can be skipped silently. There is no memo or reference binding and no payer binding. The hash is not recorded as used.

failing_checks.title: Externally supplied transactions
failing_checks.reason: The client signs a SAC transfer built from the challenge's recipient, currency and amount. Nothing checks these against an allowlist or a cap. prepareTransaction also takes the footprint and auth from the RPC without inspection. failing_checks.title: Raw byte signing
failing_checks.reason: The signed bytes are the return value of prepare_commitment. That call runs on a channel address taken from the challenge (line 63), through an RPC and network the challenge can select (line 64). The bytes are signed raw, with no prefix or structure check. failing_checks.title: Network and endpoint pinning
failing_checks.reason: The client takes the network, and with it the passphrase and the default RPC URL, from the challenge, which a counterparty controls. The same pattern is at src/channel/client/Channel.ts:64. The signing path therefore does not use operator configuration. The server paths use operator configuration.

failing_checks.title: Expiry and fees
failing_checks.reason: Transactions have timebounds, but the fee-bump max fee is 10 times the fee of a client-built transaction. That fee is not capped. The sponsor pays the resulting fees, including the Soroban resource fee.

failing_checks.title: Submission outcome
failing_checks.reason: sendResult.status (ERROR, TRY_AGAIN_LATER) is never checked. Polling has no attempt limit, so a rejected transaction hangs forever. failing_checks.title: Failure and rollback paths
failing_checks.reason: The challenge is marked used before verification and submission. Any later failure (a failed transaction, a timeout, a simulation error) burns the challenge with no rollback, so a paying client cannot retry. failing_checks.title: Verification of incoming authentication
failing_checks.reason: Push-mode verification accepts a tx hash that is not bound to the challenge or payer, and falls through when the envelope can't be checked. The same tx hash can satisfy multiple challenges when no store is set.

failing_checks.title: Controls outside the prompt
failing_checks.reason: The client signs and pays whatever amount, recipient and asset the challenge states. No code enforces a cap, an allowlist or a budget, so a model or counterparty can steer the payment.

failing_checks.title: Core function works
failing_checks.reason: Polling after submission has no attempt bound and the sendTransaction status is not checked. A rejected transaction makes the loop spin forever. The push-mode path also falls through when it cannot verify the envelope.
